internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes the notion of entities SET INTO A STRAIGHT, ORDERED, SIDE-BY-SIDE LINEAR ARRAY — a rank/row alignment in which parts are held even and extended along a line rather than heaped, scattered, or folded. The invariant is "aligned straight arraying" (linear even-order), independent of who is arrayed or what construction frames it.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all 14 occurrences the same picture recurs: things brought into an even, extended, linear order. The dominant surface form is the accusative circumstantial noun صَفًّا "(as) a row/rank": humans presented before the Lord صَفًّا (18:48), magicians told to come صَفًّا (20:64), fighters in God's way arrayed صَفًّا "like a welded structure" (61:4), angels standing صَفًّا (78:38) and rank-upon-rank صَفًّا صَفًّا (89:22, two occurrences), and the sworn "arrangers" وَٱلصَّٰٓفَّٰتِ صَفًّا (37:1, both words). The active-participle family names the agents who so array themselves: ٱلصَّآفُّونَ "we are indeed those ranged in ranks" (37:165). The passive-participle family names objects put into rows: سُرُرٍ مَّصْفُوفَةٍ "couches set in rows" (52:20) and نَمَارِقُ مَصْفُوفَةٌ "cushions arranged in rows" (88:15). The camel form صَوَآفَّ (22:36) describes sacrificial beasts drawn up standing in line. Two bird occurrences, ٱلطَّيْرُ صَٰٓفَّٰتٍ (24:41; 67:19), show the same core as extended-straight alignment: 67:19 explicitly contrasts صَٰٓفَّٰتٍ with وَيَقْبِضْنَ ("and they fold/draw in"), so صافّ = wings held out straight and even, the opposite of folding. Whether the aligned units are many bodies in a rank or the two wings of one bird held straight, the residue is identical: held even and extended along a straight line/order.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM subtracted: صَفًّا = verbal-noun/accusative used circumstantially ("in the state of a row"); ٱلصَّآفُّونَ / ٱلصَّٰٓفَّٰتِ / صَٰٓفَّٰتٍ / صَوَآفَّ = active participles (masc. pl., fem. pl., and the diptote plural صَوَافّ) naming the agents that array/extend themselves; مَّصْفُوفَة = passive participle naming the object placed into rows. CONSTRUCTION subtracted: عُرِضُوا ... صَفًّا, ٱئْتُوا صَفًّا, يُقَٰتِلُونَ ... صَفًّا, يَقُومُ ... صَفًّا all use the accusative-of-state frame supplying "in the manner of a rank"; the intensifying reduplication صَفًّا صَفًّا (89:22) supplies "rank after rank," not new root content; the قبض-contrast (67:19) is contextual antonymy. PARTICIPANTS subtracted: humans, magicians, warriors, angels, spirits, birds, camels, couches, cushions — all interchangeable carriers of the same alignment. CONTEXT subtracted: eschatological muster (18:48; 78:38; 89:22), narrative contest (20:64), sacrificial ritual (22:36), cosmic praise/flight (24:41; 67:19), oath (37:1,165), military exhortation (61:4), Paradise furnishing (52:20; 88:15). Residue after all subtraction: straight even linear arraying.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The bird occurrences صَٰٓفَّٰتٍ (24:41; 67:19). Here the surface sense could be read as "spreading wings" rather than "multiple entities in a row," which would threaten the row/rank reading. It reconciles cleanly, however, because 67:19 itself supplies the internal bridge: صَٰٓفَّٰتٍ is set against وَيَقْبِضْنَ ("and they fold in"). The contrast shows صافّ = wings held out straight and even (extended in alignment), the antonym of folding/contracting — i.e. the same "held straight and even along a line" residue, applied to the two wings of one body rather than to many bodies. So the harder case actually confirms the abstract core (straight even extension/alignment) rather than merely the concrete "crowd-in-a-line" reading.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The strongest alternative is that the core is narrowly "a row/rank of MULTIPLE entities side by side" (plurality-in-line). This fits 12 occurrences directly. Internal evidence arbitrates against restricting it that narrowly: 67:19's صَٰٓفَّٰتٍ-vs-يَقْبِضْنَ contrast makes the salient opposition straight-extension vs folding within a single flyer's wings, not merely one-vs-many. The more abstract formulation ("straight even aligned arraying") therefore subsumes the plurality-row hypothesis and additionally covers the wing cases, so internal data favors the abstract center while the concrete "rank of many" remains its most frequent realization.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest semantic neighbors: (1) رصّ rSS "weld/compact tightly together" — co-occurs in the very same verse, 61:4: صَفًّا كَأَنَّهُم بُنْيَٰنٌ مَّرْصُوصٌ, showing the language treats them as distinct layers: Sff supplies the linear rank/alignment, rSS supplies the tight leak-free welding/compaction. Sff does NOT entail compression, only even linear order. (2) نضد nDd "stack/pile in layers" (vertical tiering) — Sff is lateral side-by-side, not stacked. (3) نظم nZm "string/thread in sequence" — sequential linkage rather than parallel even alignment. (4) رتّب-type ordering — abstract ranking without the spatial straight-line image. Falsifiability: the hypothesis fails if Sff were used for a disordered heap, for tight compression without linear order, or for vertical stacking — none occur; every attestation involves even, extended, straight-line arraying.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty contribution — "entities set into a straight, even, side-by-side linear array (rank/row/held-straight alignment)" — is surface-recoverable in every one of the 14 occurrences and its direction is determinate (linear even order, not compaction, stacking, or sequence). The three form-families (accusative صَفًّا, active participles ٱلصَّآفُّونَ/صَٰٓفَّٰتٍ/صَوَآفَّ, passive مَّصْفُوفَة) and every participant class (people, angels, warriors, birds, camels, furniture) all reduce to it after subtracting form, construction, participants, and context. The only occurrences needing more than trivial reading — the birds صَٰٓفَّٰتٍ — are reconciled by an internally attested bridge (the صافّ/قبض antonymy in 67:19), which extends rather than strains the core. The root is sharply distinguished from its nearest neighbor رصّ within a shared verse (61:4), confirming its distinctive contribution is alignment-in-a-line, not compaction. No occurrence resists reconciliation, so inconsistent_refs is empty and clean universal presence is claimed; the slight abstraction needed for the wing cases keeps it just short of "trivially concrete everywhere" but well within STRONG.

adversarial_verification.notes: Refutation sweep across all 14 occurrences found no genuine failing occurrence. Clusters: (A) human/angelic ranks — 18:48, 20:64, 78:38, 89:22(x2), 37:1(x2), 37:165, 61:4 — all literal side-by-side rows/ranks; 61:4 co-locates صَفًّا with مَّرْصُوص, showing the root rides on 'row-alignment' (صفّ) as distinct from 'welded compactness' (رصّ). (B) objects set in rows — 52:20 مَّصْفُوفَة couches, 88:15 مَصْفُوفَة cushions — clean fit. (C) camels 22:36 صَوَآفّ drawn up standing in line — fit. HARDEST CASE (D): the two bird occurrences 24:41 and 67:19, where the referent is a single bird's two wings, not many entities in a rank; the candidate must widen 'side-by-side array of entities' to 'parts held straight/even and extended, not folded.' This strains the surface 'rank/row' gloss, but it is NOT a genuine semantic split: 67:19 explicitly opposes صَٰٓفَّٰت to وَيَقْبِضْن (fold/draw-in), pinning the sense to 'held-out-straight vs folded' — the same geometric invariant (even linear extension, not folded/heaped) that governs the rank cases. This is polysemy under one core, and classical usage (صفّ الطائرُ جناحيه) sits in the same root as lining-up, so no homonymy. Distinctiveness holds against nearest neighbors: رصّ (packed/welded-tight, kept explicitly separate at 61:4), نضد (stacked in tiers/layers), and قبض (folding, the direct antonym at 67:19) — صفّ = single-plane even linear extension. Falsifiable: failure = any occurrence meaning heaping, scattering, layer-stacking, or folding; none meets it, and 67:19 actively excludes folding. Verdict SUPPORTED: distinct, falsifiable, unified, no unreconciled occurrence.
